title: Carbon dioxide and temperature: what the supplied record can support
subtitle: 2022 HiMCM Problem B | Retrospective practice

pages.title: Carbon dioxide and temperature

blocks.text: Using the supplied annual Mauna Loa CO2 and global temperature records through 2021, we evaluate historical claims, compare forecast rules and examine how concentration and temperature move together. The ten-year concentration rise ending in 2004 is 18.74 ppm, slightly below 18.77 ppm ending in 2003. This small arithmetic difference does not establish physical significance, and annual observations cannot settle the statement's March-specific claim.

We compare recent drift (D), quadratic growth (Q) and exponential growth (E) using fixed chronological development forecasts. D minimizes pooled development error, but Q has lower CO2 error on the later 2012-2021 assessment. Rankings also vary across origins. We retain the prespecified selection and conclude that no uniformly best future model is established.
None reaches this pure-CO<sub>2</sub> threshold by 2050. OECD's cited 685 ppm instead measures greenhouse gases as CO<sub>2</sub>-equivalent, so the calculations do not test the same quantity. [6]

The selected sequential temperature path, T1-D, improves on the specified linear-time baseline, although T1-Q has slightly lower errors. T1-D reaches anomalies of 1.25, 1.50 and 2.00 degrees C above 1951-1980 in 2036, 2048 and 2076. These are conditional annual central-path crossings, not realized, sustained or Paris-target dates. Alternative models and fitting windows change them. Strong level association weakens after detrending and differencing; it does not identify causation.

Backtests cover at most ten years, and the selected temperature historical-error envelope misses 2016. Thus 2031 is only the corresponding display cutoff, not a validated reliability date. Neither historical envelopes nor model spread provide probability bounds for distant forecasts.

We recommend consistent measurement definitions, continued monitoring, repeated error assessment and comparison of alternative assumptions. Estimating intervention effects requires additional emissions, forcing and response evidence.

pages.deck: A bounded empirical solution to 2022 HiMCM Problem B

pages.title: A connected answer to the problem

rows: 9. Historical error envelopes and their miss

blocks.text: Approach and scope

The question has three linked tasks: check concentration claims, model the concentration-temperature relationship, and explain the implications to a public audience. We reconcile definitions, then compare simple continuations with chronological forecast tests. Concentration outputs become inputs to the linked temperature extension. [1]

All fitted observations come from the supplied historical workbook. Dates answer the mathematical exercise under explicit continuation assumptions, not an emissions-driven climate model. Tables and figures use the reviewed scientific run; exact evidence bindings and reproducible sources accompany this practice report.

The supplied workbook is the sole numerical input. Its two sheets contain 63 annual CO<sub>2</sub> observations and 64 annual temperature anomalies. Admission checked every stored cell, printed tables and year keys; no missing values or years, duplicates or nonnumeric observations were found. We preserve the supplied vintage through 2021 rather than substitute revised live data. [1,2]

rows: Annual dry-air mole fraction at Mauna Loa, Hawaii; ppm
Global land-ocean anomaly; degrees C relative to 1951-1980
Inner join on calendar year; 63 matched observations

blocks.text: The temperature-only 1958 observation is retained in its source table but excluded from the common modeling sample. A positional join would mismatch years. Negative anomalies are valid. Mauna Loa is an atmospheric indicator, while temperature is a global index; their spatial definitions differ. NASA's index combines land-air and sea-surface temperature anomalies. [2,5]
Annual observations do not become March observations

The statement's March caption conflicts with its annual-mean source and supplied values. We interpret the modeling series as annual. It can answer the supported annual comparison but cannot directly verify or disprove a March-specific record or claims about all earlier history. [1,3]
May 2022 and the OECD benchmark
NOAA's June 2022 release gives May monthly means of 420.99 ppm (NOAA) and 420.78 ppm (Scripps), supporting rounded 421 ppm. This monthly Mauna Loa context is excluded from fitting and validation. [4]

OECD's approximately 685 ppm in 2050 denotes greenhouse gases in CO<sub>2</sub>-equivalent under a conditional baseline. Its separate CO<sub>2</sub>-only levels are approximately 530 ppm in 2050 and 780 ppm in 2100. We retain the requested pure-CO<sub>2</sub> exercise without presenting a mismatch as a test of OECD's different quantity. [6]

blocks.title: Temperature baseline
blocks.text: The 1.25, 1.50 and 2.00 degree thresholds are above the 1951-1980 mean. No pre-industrial conversion is made; these are not Paris-target dates. [1,5]

pages.title: The annual 2004 rise was not the largest

blocks.text: A ten-year interval contains ten elapsed years, so we compare endpoints rather than count ten listed observations. The increase and annualized rate are
Delta<sub>10,t</sub> = C<sub>t</sub> - C<sub>t-10</sub>;     g<sub>10,t</sub> = Delta<sub>10,t</sub>/10.

blocks.caption: Figure 1. All supported ten-year annual changes ending 1969-2004. The two latest windows are nearly equal. Source: accepted ten_year_changes table; observations [2].

blocks.text: The 2004 window ranks second among the 36 supported intervals ending 1969-2004. Its increase is 0.03 ppm below the earlier maximum ending in 2003. Therefore we do not agree that 2004 is strictly largest in the supplied annual series.

blocks.title: What this answer does not establish
blocks.text: The 0.03-ppm margin is arithmetic, not evidence of a physically significant difference. Annual data do not settle the actual March assertion, and the supplied coverage cannot test every earlier historical period.

Write x = (year - 1959)/10 and C<sub>ref</sub> = 315.98 ppm. One x-unit is a decade. Only observations available through each origin enter estimation. Least squares uses a stable SVD solution; full precision is retained for forecasts and crossings. Display coefficients are rounded.
D: continue recent absolute growth

D anchors at the latest concentration and uses average annual growth between 2011 and 2021. Generally, s<sub>o</sub> = (C<sub>o</sub> - C<sub>o-10</sub>)/10 and C<sub>D</sub>(t|o) = C<sub>o</sub> + s<sub>o</sub>(t-o). It is a recent-growth forecast baseline, not an explanation fitted to the whole history.
Q: continue constant absolute acceleration
Q fits concentration to 1, x and x squared. Its quadratic coefficient is not constrained to force acceleration. Turning points and nonpositive extrapolated concentrations must remain visible.
E: continue constant proportional growth

E fits log(C/C<sub>ref</sub>) to a linear trend. Its fit loss is in log units, but predictive comparisons use ppm. No lognormal error model or mean correction is assumed. Q and E use all 63 years for the production refit.

Q follows the historical curve more closely than E, but both retain persistent residual patterns. D's smaller fit error covers only 11 observations and cannot be ranked against 63-point errors as if the samples matched. Forecast errors, not this fit table, determine selection.

pages.title: A selected rule is not a universal winner

blocks.text: Development origins are 1981, 1986, 1991, 1996 and 2001, each at horizons 1-10. The 50 overlapping origin-target pairs end no later than 2011. Selection minimizes pooled mean absolute error (MAE); RMSE and signed bias describe further behavior. Numerical ties follow D, E, Q.
MAE = mean(|prediction - observation|);     RMSE = sqrt(mean(error<super>2</super>)).

blocks.caption: Figure 2. The later assessment reverses the D-versus-Q ranking. Final predictions originate in 2011 and target 2012-2021 without intermediate refitting. Units are ppm.

blocks.text: Q is most accurate of these three on the later 2012-2021 assessment. D remains the prespecified pooled-development choice. Q wins three development origins; D wins two. Omitting either 1986 or 1991 changes the pooled diagnostic winner to Q. These post-assessment stability summaries do not replace the original selector.

D underpredicts every final CO<sub>2</sub> observation, with a ten-year error of -4.07 ppm. No uniform superiority or known future winner is established. A separate production step refits unchanged forms through 2021; matching the benchmark is never a selection criterion.

pages.title: Concentration projections depend on the rule

blocks.caption: Figure 3. Observations end in 2021; colored lines are full-window conditional extensions. The reference is the requested pure-CO2 threshold, not OECD CO2-equivalent.

blocks.text: None reaches 685 ppm by 2050. Q first reaches it in 2100, D in 2131 and E in 2136. These are first integer annual central-path crossings under the fitted continuation, not forecasts validated at those dates.

The spread grows from 30.52 ppm in 2050 to 104.63 ppm in 2100. Divergence reflects the absolute-growth, acceleration and proportional-growth assumptions. It is sensitivity across these models, not a probability interval or bound on all plausible futures.

blocks.title: Source and horizon caution
blocks.text: OECD reports a different quantity, CO2-equivalent. [6] Tests of at most ten-year forecasts cannot validate these distant values. Numerical digits reproduce model arithmetic, not future measurement precision.

pages.title: Forecast concentration enters the temperature model

blocks.text: Temperature T is an anomaly in degrees C relative to 1951-1980. We compare a linear-time baseline with a descriptive log-concentration relationship over the same paired training years. Production coefficients through 2021 give

T0 measures what this specified full-history linear trend predicts. T1 associates equal proportional concentration changes with equal changes in fitted anomaly. Its slope is not identified climate sensitivity or a causal policy-effect coefficient.
Validate the entire linked forecast

At origin o, T1's coefficients use observed paired data through o. Future temperature substitutes forecast C from D, Q or E; realized future concentration never enters its score. Temperature error therefore includes upstream concentration error. An invalid path cannot be rescued with future observations.
T1-m(t|o) = alpha<sub>o</sub> + beta<sub>o</sub> log(C<sub>m</sub>(t|o)/C<sub>ref</sub>).

The sequential rule first selects D, then compares T0 with T1-D. T1-D wins that eligible comparison. T1-Q has slightly lower errors among all declared comparators. We retain this fact rather than call the selected pipeline a global minimum.

T1-D improves on the specified linear-time baseline in both periods. This does not establish unique CO<sub>2</sub> information beyond every representation of time. Substituting exponential E into T1 gives alpha + beta a + beta b x: a straight line in future time despite different calibration.

pages.title: Temperature dates are conditional annual crossings

blocks.caption: Figure 4. Full-window extensions and observed anomalies relative to 1951-1980. Markers label selected T1-D crossings. Every threshold date is beyond the ten-year tested horizon from 2021.

blocks.text: The direct answer for selected T1-D is 2036, 2048 and 2076. Alternative concentration assumptions move the linked dates; T0 gives 2044, 2059 and 2089. The last two columns are anomalies, not absolute temperatures.

A crossing is the first integer year after 2021 whose unrounded central-path value reaches the threshold, searched through 2300. It is not the first realized warm year or the start of sustained warming. T0 in 2088 is 1.999310 C, which displays as 2.00 but is below 2; its crossing is correctly 2089.

blocks.title: No change of baseline or certainty
blocks.text: These dates refer to the 1951-1980 mean, not pre-industrial warming or Paris targets. They are conditional arithmetic, not probability quantiles, established deadlines or validated century-scale forecasts.

pages.title: A strong association is not causal identification

blocks.caption: Figure 5. Left: levels with the accepted log-concentration fitted curve. Right: accepted annual changes. The panels answer different descriptive questions; neither establishes causation.

blocks.text: The indicators rise together strongly at level. The log-concentration fit has descriptive R-squared 0.922302. This does not mean CO2 caused 92.2% of warming. Removing separate linear or quadratic time trends weakens the association; annual changes weaken it further.

Detrending and differencing change the question and remove low-frequency information. Weaker correlations neither disprove a physical greenhouse mechanism nor identify its magnitude. Omitted forcings, response delays, serial dependence and the station/global spatial mismatch prevent these two series from isolating cause.

These are the primary 1959-2021 diagnostics (1960-2021 for changes), not earlier exploratory values from a shorter period. We report descriptive relationships without independent-observation p-values or a causal climate-sensitivity interpretation.

pages.title: The historical envelope misses a later temperature observation

blocks.text: For the selected pipeline at horizon h, take the largest absolute development error across all five origins and all horizons j no greater than h. This gives a nondecreasing historical error reference:
B<sub>h</sub> = max |error<sub>o,j</sub>|, over development origins o and 1 <= j <= h.

blocks.caption: Figure 6. Fixed development-derived envelopes assessed on forecasts from 2011. The selected temperature path misses 2016. Shading is a historical-error reference, not a calibrated confidence or prediction interval.

blocks.text: D's reference contains all ten later CO<sub>2</sub> observations; T1-D contains nine of ten later temperatures. We retain the 2016 miss and do not enlarge the radius afterward. Ten temporally related checks are not independent trials, and 9/10 containment does not estimate 90% future coverage.
The miss directly contradicts a guaranteed-bound interpretation. We keep it beside the principal temperature forecast, including in the summary and article.

pages.title: How far can the model be trusted?

blocks.text: The tests cover only horizons one to ten years, with five development origins per horizon. The final errors below belong to predictions made in 2011 and checked against 2012, 2016 and 2021. They are not measured errors in 2022, 2026 or 2031.

From 2021, the same ten-year maximum ends in 2031. This is a tested-horizon display cutoff, not a validated reliability date. There are 50 development pairs but only 30 distinct target years. Dependence and the small final sample limit generalization. No accuracy tolerance supplied by the question identifies a universal reliable-through year.
Sensitivity to the fitting window

The predeclared sensitivity refits selected forms on 1992-2021. D is unchanged because its last-ten-year rule is unchanged; this does not establish robustness of the whole linked framework. The refitted T1-D association changes:

Dates move 3, 4 and 8 years earlier. This is not a new chosen model, confidence interval or retuned selector. Form changes also matter: linked 2100 anomalies span 2.21685-2.83946 C; adding T0 gives 2.20113-2.83946 C.

blocks.title: Practical reliability answer
blocks.text: Use short-horizon errors as limited conditional evidence and reassess as observations arrive. All 2050/2100 values and distant crossings depend on continuation assumptions; neither this sample nor the envelopes establishes a guaranteed reliable horizon.
What the architecture does well

The models are transparent, use few parameters and represent distinct continuation assumptions. Evaluation respects information available at each origin. Linked temperature scores include concentration forecast error. A fixed selector, explicit alternatives, residual diagnostics and adverse results make the answer inspectable rather than dependent on a single fitted curve.

rows: Endpoint growth can be unrepresentative; later errors expose underprediction.
Curvature can dominate distant behavior; a better later score does not certify 2100.
An empirical continuation, not an emissions/sink mechanism.
Omits lags and other drivers; coefficient is descriptive, not causal.
Tests do not recreate the exact data vintage available to historical forecasters.
No independent-trial or calibrated probability interpretation.

blocks.text: Mathematical validity is narrower than credibility

All actual full and declared last-30 paths are finite, valid and nondecreasing over the annual search domain 2021-2300. Reported crossings satisfy unrounded boundaries; the supplied history never exceeds the requested levels. These facts establish calculation status, not climate credibility through 2300.

First-passage inference uses only the contiguous valid prefix from the origin. A crossing before later invalidity is retained with a warning; invalidity before crossing blocks a date. Already-above-origin and valid non-crossing-through-2300 cases have different statuses. No later valid segment bridges an invalid gap.
Why not simply add complexity?

High-degree curves add extrapolation flexibility without long-horizon evidence. A logistic capacity is not identified by this rising record. Physical carbon-cycle and energy-balance models need emissions, sinks, forcing and response inputs absent from the two supplied series. These justify a bounded exercise, not an exhaustive-model claim.

blocks.text: Use the findings without overstating them
Keep measurements comparable. Preserve the annual/monthly distinction, temperature baseline, data vintage and CO2-equivalent definition before interpreting a quoted number.

Monitor performance and compare assumptions. Preserve the chosen rule for an honest assessment, track later errors and show competing paths. Ranking reversals and envelope misses should prompt reassessment, not disappear.

Use more evidence for intervention decisions. Planning can compare conclusions under different assumptions. Quantifying a policy's effect requires emissions, forcings, sinks and response dynamics that these two records do not identify.

These recommendations follow from definition conflicts, ranking instability and extrapolation sensitivity. We do not estimate a specific intervention's benefit or assign probabilities to distant scenarios.

pages.title: Climate numbers need more than a date

blocks.text: A concentration figure can be accurate yet answer the wrong question. We examined the records supplied through 2021 for a mathematical modeling exercise, beginning with what each number measures.

The supplied CO<sub>2</sub> values are annual Mauna Loa averages, despite the question's reference to March. Their ten-year rise ending in 2004 was 18.74 parts per million, slightly below 18.77 ppm ending in 2003. That small difference does not settle the separate March claim. NOAA's source supports about 421 ppm for the monthly average in May 2022; this later observation was not used to fit our models. [1-4]

Three simple extensions of past concentration changes produce roughly 466-497 ppm in 2050 and 584-688 ppm in 2100. None reaches 685 ppm by 2050. This does not refute OECD: its cited figure combines greenhouse gases as CO2-equivalent, rather than measuring CO2 alone. [6]

The model changes the answer. A recent-growth rule performed best in our planned development comparison, but a quadratic curve performed better on the later 2012-2021 assessment. Neither has demonstrated universal superiority. We retain the original selection rather than choose again after seeing those errors.

Our selected temperature path, driven by recent-growth CO2, reaches 1.25, 1.50 and 2.00 degrees C above the 1951-1980 average in 2036, 2048 and 2076. Driving the same relationship with the quadratic concentration path gives slightly smaller errors. Other models and fitting periods move the dates. These are conditional paths, not established deadlines, sustained warming dates or Paris targets. The observed association also does not isolate cause.
Tests extend only ten years ahead, and the temperature error reference missed 2016. They establish no guaranteed reliability date or probability for a century-scale projection.

The useful response is continued measurement, consistent definitions and regular comparison of forecasts with observations. Planning should examine several assumptions. Evaluating interventions additionally requires evidence on emissions, other climate drivers and response delays; these two records cannot quantify policy benefits.

Practice and AI use

This is a retrospective exercise, not a live entry or external submission. Codex collaboration sessions carried out coordination, source/data admission, modeling, computation, writing/visuals and independent review, with some roles operating sequentially. The user delegated reversible practice decisions to the coordinator; no human checkpoint response or Claude Code execution is invented.

The companion project retains source/model versions, commands, fixed outputs and claim bindings. Scientific run T05-scientific-20261103-r03 supplies this report. Independent numerical review accepted this run and scoped claims. Plots and tables read accepted outputs without refitting. Writer rendering checks are author self-checks, not independent PDF acceptance.
Evaluation exposure and repairs

Candidate forms and the selector were fixed before adversarial final-score exposure. An adversarial reviewer nevertheless examined 2012-2021 scores before the primary selection receipt. The primary run retained local selection-before-assessment order, but the project has no globally unseen or blind holdout. Later interpretation and implementation safeguards are post-exposure repairs, not a fresh evaluation.

Earlier failed artifacts and repaired versions are retained. The producer reports 44 implementation tests and byte-identical reproduction of 32 numerical outputs from 88 recovered dependencies; these are execution evidence, not proof of future accuracy. Separate recovery and final PDF review have their own acceptance records; this report does not claim their completion in advance.
